card.name: Mwomboko
card.profile: Mwomboko is a Kikuyu social partner dance of central Kenya that emerged in the colonial era, traced to roughly the late 1930s and 1940s (The Standard). It is danced in pairs with methodical, counted steps resembling a waltz or slow foxtrot, prominently featuring the accordion (kinanda kia mugeto) and the karing'aring'a (a metal ring idiophone). The style developed after veterans returning from the World Wars brought back accordions and guitars, and after the colonial ban on the protest dance Muthirigu pushed the community toward a tolerated substitute.
card.insight: Originally a dance for unmarried young men, mwomboko was later adopted by elders and is now showcased at Kenyan national celebrations such as Madaraka and Mashujaa Day; veterans like Wachira Waweru have warned the accordion-driven genre risks dying out (The Standard).
card.image_significance: Kikuyu foxtrot of the accordion. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — Kikuyu, Kenya.
